h: Fairy-tale castles and a few wild putts
p: If you've done the city-centre castle and fancy another, Castell Coch is a real treat. It sits in the woods above Tongwynlais, just north of Cardiff, and looks like something straight out of a fairy tale, with its pointed red towers rebuilt in Victorian times. A morning there and an afternoon of adventure golf makes for a properly well-rounded family day.

St Fagans National Museum of History, on the western edge of the city, is another must. It's an open-air museum full of historic buildings brought from all over Wales and rebuilt on site, from farmhouses to a whole row of miners' cottages. Back in the centre, National Museum Cardiff in Cathays Park has art, natural history and dinosaurs to keep everyone busy.

For the golf itself, allow around an hour. Booking ahead means you can slot it neatly around a match or a show, and arriving a little early avoids any stress. Keep the scorecard simple, let the youngest players go first, and maybe introduce a forfeit for whoever finishes last, such as buying the Welsh cakes on the way home.

Speaking of which, Cardiff Market, the Victorian indoor market off St Mary Street, is a great place to grab some Welsh cakes or a snack. And if the weather is kind, Barry Island's beach is just a short train ride away for a seaside finish.
